title: Open Course — Modular Theory & Weights
description: A research-level course developing integration and comparison for general weights, modular symmetry, standard forms, spatial derivatives, correspondences and expectations.

topic_routes.title: Closing involutions and the modular theorem
topic_routes.route_description: Follow the closed involution through the two multiplication actions, bounded approximation and analytic domains to the modular commutant theorem.

topic_routes.title: Relative modular and spatial derivatives
topic_routes.route_description: Use standard forms and closed positive forms to construct spatial energies, relative Tomita operators and their support corners.

topic_routes.title: Modular flows, KMS and centralizers
topic_routes.route_description: Characterize modular time by its boundary condition, identify the fixed algebra, and study invariant weights and equilibrium states.

topic_routes.title: Changing weights and Connes cocycles
topic_routes.route_description: Compare weights through supported relative data, prove composition and reconstruction, then study domains and continuity.

topic_routes.title: Measurable operators and trace integration
topic_routes.route_description: Construct measurable operators with their domains, extend the trace, prove the integration and duality results, and pass to general nontracial Lp spaces.

topic_routes.title: Expectations and operator-valued weights
topic_routes.route_description: Begin with contractive retractions and the modular invariance criterion. Continue through extended positives, operator-valued integration, commutant duality and expectation index.

topic_routes.title: Plancherel weights, tensor products and disintegration
topic_routes.route_description: Construct group weights and tensor weights, then assemble measurable Hilbert spaces and weight fields with their stated countability hypotheses.

learning_outcomes: Construct finite weight domains and semicyclic representations without assuming a faithful normal state.
Prove and distinguish bounded comparison, relative modular, spatial derivative and Connes cocycle constructions with precise domains.
Derive modular symmetry, standard forms, measurable integration, fusion and expectations in their full stated generality.
Distinguish the uses of normality, semifiniteness, support, topology and convergence, and recognize insufficient special cases.

For general groups: integrated representations, nonunital positive-functional GNS, continuous positive-definite coefficients and finite kernel matrices. The full group dual is the Fourier–Stieltjes Banach algebra, the regular Fourier algebra is its contractive ideal, and the weak* topology on group C*-states is compact-uniform convergence. The VII.3 measure exercises construct an invariant measure from a quasi-invariant standard Borel measure class, distinguish arbitrary from strict derivative versions, prove uniqueness of invariant measures, and derive a Borel modular homomorphism. The printed arbitrary-version diagonal claim is explicitly refuted. The remaining VII.3 exercises recover a compatible locally compact topology from a nonzero invariant measure, identify the group-like operators, and exclude nonzero quasi-invariant measures on infinite-dimensional norm-Borel Hilbert spaces of arbitrary dimension and on the strong-topology unitary groups of arbitrary infinite-dimensional factors in faithful normal representations. Zero-measure and unstated-topology source defects are recorded. The regular Fourier predual embeds isometrically as a closed ideal in the Fourier–Stieltjes algebra, with an exact bidual central-carrier criterion. Positive coefficient nets converge uniformly on compact sets precisely when their positive functionals converge weak* and their masses converge; two solved examples separate the norms and exhibit loss of mass. An exact compact-representation theorem import with a factor-specific compression argument proves that a strongly compact unitary group forces a factor to be finite dimensional; matrix and diagonal-torus examples explain the factor condition.

lessons.summary: Full measurable-corner modular domains and spectra, return-witness subgroup and density arguments, ergodic reduction invariance, and equality of the asymptotic ratio set with the all-weight modular invariant including zero.

lessons.title: Relation symmetries and weight covariance
lessons.summary: Relation symmetries with their diagonal phases, standard unitaries at infinite mass, transported finite weight ideals, full relative modular domains and normalized cocycles, with exact earlier proofs of reconstruction and the closed geometric group.

lessons.title: Relation cores and lifted symmetries
lessons.summary: The full lifted-relation core with its normalized trace; canonical extensions of diagonal-preserving symmetries, exact measure-change coordinates, unbounded core density domains and the induced center flow.

lessons.title: Relation factors, traces and corners
lessons.summary: Complete orbit-field and factor-type criteria, atomicity of expected diagonals in type I factors, invariant traces and finite measurable corners, normalized corner cocycles and countably infinite atomic cores.

lessons.title: Orbit quotients and modular types
lessons.summary: Full Polish orbit and measurable quotient criteria with exact earlier proofs; controlled averaging to nonsingular probabilities, bounded derivatives, entire modular orbit generators, and the universal type I criterion for countable actions.

lessons.title: Groupoid reductions and modular matrix blocks
lessons.summary: Full algebraic and countable Borel reductions and presentations; sigma-finite finite-sheet measures, matrix weights, full relative modular domains, entire cutoffs and normalized corners.

lessons.title: Measured comparison, returns and modular amplification
lessons.summary: Full measured comparison and both splitting and return theorems; concrete modular amplification, sheet-density weights, maximal relative domains, normalized corners and entire partial-orbit cutoffs.

lessons.title: Dyadic approximation and modular weights
lessons.summary: Full dyadic approximation and nonsingular towers, compatible scalar matrices, original-weight modular fields, weight-preserving expectations and relative graph-domain convergence.

lessons.title: Cohomology, lifting and modular reweighting
lessons.summary: Measurable lifts, stabilized cohomology corrections, full almost-everywhere flow reduction, countable-range modular reweighting, eigenspaces and maximal relative domains.

lessons.title: Ancillary actions and modular transport
lessons.summary: Variable-field ancillary conjugacy, full stabilizer splitting, noncommutative defect repair, free-centre classification and complete weight and modular-domain transport.

lessons.title: Groupoid exercises and modular consequences
lessons.summary: Dense and two-gap roofs, irrational Weyl-factor approximation, cocycle and semidirect groupoids, uniform localization, abelian stabilizers and modular asymptotic ranges.

lessons.title: Haar amenability and modular averaging
lessons.summary: Invariant Haar means, compact convex fixed points, all Reiter formulations, compact Folner sets, regular coefficients and faithful group norms, with normal state-preserving averages and complete modular domains.

lessons.title: Amenable extensions and radical obstructions
lessons.summary: Closed-subgroup transfer, normal extensions, solvable examples, unrestricted connected Lie quotients and the full almost-connected radical criterion, with successive modular averaging.

lessons.title: Measured amenability and finite approximation
lessons.summary: Invariant means, weighted finite-patch construction, hyperfiniteness and constant-size arrays, nonsingular finite-dimensional crossed-product approximation, isotropy counterexamples, coherent inner corrections and maximal modular domains.

lessons.title: Infinite products and modular time
lessons.summary: Pointed Hilbert products and normal GNS kernels, corrected phase convergence, arbitrary concrete commutants, maximal modular domains, nonfaithful support corners, exact product-innerness and the full separable-factor semifiniteness criterion.

lessons.title: Inductive limits and quasi-free factors
lessons.summary: Noninjective inductive limits and properness, CAR matrix units and simplicity, exterior Fock space, every quasi-free covariance, full reduced GNS factoriality, bounded AFD approximation, product states and the all-weight type III parameter, with explicit source convention corrections.

lessons.title: Spectral cuts and irreducible centralizers
lessons.summary: Real spectral cuts, semicircle estimates, state independence of trivial bicentralizers, matrix central-vector standard forms, successive finite matrix reductions and faithful states with irreducible centralizer, with corrected constants and normalization.

lessons.title: Narrow modular spectra and projection displacement
lessons.summary: Dominant-weight scalar averaging, exact narrow modular spectral support, matrix-column displacement, both functional-domination cases, selfadjoint reduction and projection extraction with source constants.

lessons.title: Projection partitions and dominant centralizers
lessons.summary: Exhaustive projection partitions, finite sign averaging, uniform displacement, and the complete equivalence of dominant-weight scalar averaging, trivial bicentralizers and irreducible state centralizers.

lessons.title: Bicentralizer structure and injective factors
lessons.summary: Von Neumann algebra and modular structure of the bicentralizer, equal-mass projection exclusion with the full atomicity argument, exact scalar-averaging criteria, and the injective type III1 application through finite-dimensional dominant-centralizer averages.

lessons.title: Directed quotients and approximate innerness
lessons.summary: A directed finite quotient and cofinal reindexing argument prove the local approximate-innerness criterion for every type III factor with a faithful normal state, without assuming separable predual.

lessons.title: Homogeneous groupoid matchings and weighted arrays
lessons.summary: Exact homogeneous matchings, compatible weighted arrays and a conditional coding theorem, with an explicit distinction between dense ratio sets and discrete-kernel ergodicity.

lessons.title: Ratio products and cyclic groupoid reductions
lessons.summary: The irrational product theorem for measured groupoids, exact essential-degree criteria, and cyclic inverse-image types with the necessary generator-occurrence hypothesis.

lessons.title: Generating weighted arrays and groupoid isomorphisms
lessons.summary: Relative realization of weighted arrays, exact refinements generating every measurable set and relation arrow, and the measure-preserving isomorphism theorem at explicit normalization hypotheses.

lessons.title: Type III1 normalization by weighted arrays
lessons.summary: Constructing an equivalent probability with prescribed exact degrees and ergodic modulus kernel, then proving type III1 measured-groupoid uniqueness by compatible weighted arrays.

lessons.title: Hypercentral sequences in the type III1 factor
lessons.summary: Centralizer block swaps, a state-preserving tail projection, ordinary and ultrafilter displacement witnesses, and the II1 factor property of central sequence algebras in the AFD III1 factor.

lessons.title: Matching weighted matrix units by approximately inner maps
lessons.summary: Exact weighted matrix matching, normal quotient comparison, a two-sided approximately inner limit, and tensor-factor conjugacy with an explicit complement hypothesis and counterexample.

lessons.title: Approximately inner automorphisms of the type III1 factor
lessons.summary: The full approximate-innerness theorem for all automorphisms of the AFD type III1 factor: retained tensor complements, replica swaps, state correction and explicit normal-functional convergence.

lessons.title: Centrally trivial automorphisms and modular time
lessons.summary: The full centrally trivial classification: weighted phase extraction, exact modular splitting, a nonvanishing central sequence, period arithmetic and a tensor-slice proof.

lessons.title: Outer conjugacy and modular invariants
lessons.summary: All outer-conjugacy classes of automorphisms of the AFD type III1 factor: unique modular time, finite-period phase, complete normal forms and dominant-weight normalization.

lessons.title: Finite-index bounded vectors and module bases
lessons.summary: Finite-index bounded-vector domains, norm comparison in every normal representation, supported module bases and equality of the expectation and tracial dimension indices.

lessons.title: Separable modular subalgebras and preserving expectations
lessons.summary: Separable modular subalgebras, coherent expectations, normal finite-model reductions, exact programme proofs for injectivity and nuclear biduals, and the sharp obstruction to using operator norms in predual matrix models.

lessons.title: The range of the index of an expectation
lessons.summary: Finite-level Markov traces inside general expectation towers, positivity below four, exact index realization and solved endpoint checks.

lessons.title: Centralizer partitions and abelian approximation
lessons.summary: Centralizer partition expectations, arbitrary directed abelian limits, relative commutants in corners, geometric pinching and equal-trace abelian approximation.

lessons.title: Bilinear state bounds and sharp finite matrix examples
lessons.summary: Four-state bounds, an exact finite-matrix optimum d/(d+1), explicit attaining states, the corrected truncation residual, and complete programme proof routes through the bilinear inequality.

lessons.title: State-weighted adjoints and modular compatibility
lessons.summary: Positive symmetric state adjoints, an exact modular-covariance criterion for GNS adjoints, a two-level counterexample, support corners, and the full finite-tracial theorem with corrected density normalization.

lessons.title: Rational state records and exact coherence loss
lessons.summary: Explicit finite state records, exact coherence coefficients and sharp commutator error; a continuous return semigroup and completely bounded rational-state perturbation with two source corrections.

lessons.title: Trace-preserving models and unitary rounding
lessons.summary: Exact trace-preserving finite models, improved adjoint and unitary-rounding bounds, and a conditional-expectation limit with an explicit obstruction to preserving approximation quality.

lessons.title: Balanced Kraus completion and coupling energy
lessons.summary: Exact positive-defect matching, balanced normal Kraus completion with a cb norm bound, and unitary coupling energy with its variance decomposition and composition rule.

lessons.title: Unitary couplings and finite-factor approximation
lessons.summary: Finite phase sampling and spectral clipping yield a uniform unitary-coupling theorem, with full tracial-ultraproduct and central-comparison arguments and the finite-factor local AFD deduction.

lessons.title: Injective corners and AFD descent
lessons.summary: Corner retractions, explicit semifinite matrix coordinates, measurable central assembly and exact containment prove the injective-to-AFD conclusion and the structure of every von Neumann subalgebra of the hyperfinite finite factor.

lessons.title: Small-corner construction and finite injectivity
lessons.summary: Invariant-state spectral levels, bounded finite-rank models, corrected polar and Gram repair, two-parameter corner selection and orthogonal-block maximality give the complete second finite-injectivity proof.

lessons.title: Strong approximation and matrix compressions
lessons.summary: Strong unitary approximation converts completely positive finite models into internal matrix algebras; resolvent membership and exact retention produce nested dyadic presentations, with corrected central trace rounding.

lessons.title: Markov expectations and coefficient recovery
lessons.summary: Markov trace coordinates give coefficient recovery for finite inclusions with centers. Uniform matrix bounds yield a completely positive lower bound for the expectation; supported bases and a sharp two-column example make the formulas explicit.

lessons.title: Finite chains of Jones projections
lessons.summary: Finite spanning windows bound nonzero Jones-projection chains between the allowed parameters. Polynomial and stabilization proofs are accompanied by the full two-projection normal form, with arbitrary multiplicity, bisector coordinates and the common-kernel summand.

lessons.title: Small expectations of projections
lessons.summary: A trace estimate for noncommuting projection intersections turns small squared L2 expectations into small operator-norm expectations. For II1 inclusions, the infimum over nonzero projections is the reciprocal Jones index, with its precise attainment criterion. A prescribed spectral cutoff also rounds a positive contraction in every normal-state seminorm, including zero defect without faithfulness.

lessons.title: Free-group norm averages with arbitrary substitute words
lessons.summary: Two partitions of free reduced words give the exact 2||x||/sqrt(N) norm bound for every admissible substitute, arbitrary generator cardinality and simultaneous finite supports.

lessons.title: Residual subgroups and uniform group-factor estimates
lessons.summary: Amalgamated normal forms construct tail groups and their separable II1 factors. Cover and disjointness estimates give the uniform constant100 bound for all finite tensor powers and Hilbert-valued coefficients.

lessons.title: Residual tails and tracial ultraproducts
lessons.summary: Uniform relative commutants and moving tails establish residual nets and residual pairs in tracial ultraproducts. Cofinal interleaving proves that depth is intrinsic and transfers through intermediate algebras.

lessons.title: A continuum of separable type II₁ factors
lessons.summary: A free-pair estimate, permutation transport and the residual-pair induction recover every binary coordinate from the ultrapower. Trace uniqueness then separates a continuum of separable typeII1 factors.

lessons.title: Free-tree representations and projections
lessons.summary: A comparison of tree vertices and edges produces a trace-class obstruction to nontrivial projections in the reduced free-group C-star algebra.

lessons.title: Dyadic subfactors and ultrafilter limits
lessons.summary: Compatible dyadic corners embed the hyperfinite factor; ultrafilter characters and binary tensor tails give explicit nonseparable central-sequence algebras.

lessons.title: Null sequences and hypercentral commutants
lessons.summary: Null-sequence tests force the multiplier condition; exact quotient identities separate the two hypercentral conventions and identify them in the finite tracial case.

lessons.title: Local projection tests for outer automorphisms
lessons.summary: Outer automorphisms admit almost disjoint projections; proper outerness is equivalent to the corresponding test in every corner, without a finiteness or countability restriction.

lessons.title: Fixed central sequences determine an automorphism
lessons.summary: For an aperiodic automorphism of the hyperfinite II1 factor, pointwise fixation of its central-sequence fixed algebra characterizes its integer powers modulo inner automorphisms.

lessons.title: Centre-valued characteristic data
lessons.summary: Implementing lifts give centre-valued characteristic pairs and an equivariant extension. Explicit gauge maps, real-flow identities and genuine-cocycle calculations prove the invariant comparison under normal transport.

lessons.title: Quotient cocycles and reconstruction
lessons.summary: Quotient sections retain subgroup cocycles. Exact associator and relative commutant arguments turn the comparison defect into a quotient cocycle and reconstruct all group coefficients from a supplied correction.

lessons.title: Finite matrix averaging and cohomology
lessons.summary: Finite matrix averaging gives uniform cocycle error bounds. An explicit finite-test diagonal proves exact and relative second-cohomology vanishing for semiliftable amenable actions on typeII central sequence algebras.

lessons.title: Core continuity and cocycle comparison
lessons.summary: Core continuity and exact characteristic phases identify mixed coefficients. Predual estimates place the quotient defect in the central sequence algebra, where second cohomology gives simultaneous automorphism and cocycle approximation.

lessons.title: Approximate first cohomology
lessons.summary: Finite tower corrections solve approximate first-cocycle equations while controlling predual commutators. The proof constructs exact unitary representatives, retains arbitrary positive functional norms, and gives ordinary sequential correction.

lessons.title: Two-sided intertwining and cocycle limits
lessons.summary: An alternating construction produces limits of conjugating automorphisms and their inverses, unitary coefficients, and exact cocycle identities on the entire group. The theorem retains both cocycles and the quotient section defect at explicitly aligned normal-subgroup hypotheses.

lessons.title: Characteristic classes and subgroup alignment
lessons.summary: Characteristic classes of normalized cocycle actions give exact subgroup alignment through central changes of core implementers and an arbitrary unitary cochain. The real-flow coefficients put the aligning unitaries in the original algebra. The intertwining consequence retains its explicit analytic hypotheses.

lessons.title: Cyclic normalization and Bernoulli relations
lessons.summary: A bounded diagonal density gives the exact cyclic modulus. Homogeneous matchings and compatible weighted arrays identify the entire measured relation with the specified binary model, including its normal group-measure-space realization.

lessons.title: Irrational modular times and tail witnesses
lessons.summary: Paired tail matrix units give exact asymptotic periods for modular time on one tensor factor. The proof covers every faithful state, the rational boundary and the normal outer-conjugacy factorization for irrational time.

lessons.title: Modular returns and comparison through the discrete core
lessons.summary: Two commuting maps on the semifinite discrete core determine modular-return invariants. Their characteristic comparison constructs normal outer conjugacy for finite and zero return, and explicit models realize every compatible tuple.

lessons.title: Odometer carries and realization of a measured flow
lessons.summary: Signed odometer carries construct a nonsingular transformation whose lifted invariant algebra carries a prescribed measured flow. Full coordinate and measure calculations give an AF principal relation and its type III0 factor.

lessons.title: Classification by the flow of weights
lessons.summary: Measurable core fibres, trace normalization and exact unitary cocycles identify AFD type III0 factors with conjugate flows and give abelian integer crossed-product models.

lessons.title: Full-group approximation of relation normalizers
lessons.summary: Balanced matrix arrays and growing finite corners characterize the closure of the full group; a continuous homomorphism records the scaling of the invariant measure.

lessons.title: Return bands and semifinite components
lessons.summary: Explicit return bands give a commuting integer action, its invariant base and exact measure derivatives; conditional measures and the continuous core identify the type II-infinity components.

lessons.title: Orbit equivalence from the associated flow
lessons.summary: The properly ergodic associated flow classifies a type III hyperfinite measured relation through measurable diagonal-pair identifications, normalized return cocycles and orbit matching.

lessons.title: Equivariant discrete decomposition
lessons.summary: A module-trivial type III0 automorphism admits a discrete presentation preserving the coefficient trace and fixing the implementing unitary, with an explicit inner correction and a lacunary dual weight.

lessons.title: Module triviality and inner approximation
lessons.summary: For a separable AFD type III0 factor, trivial module is equivalent to approximate innerness. Finite return classes give coherent implementers and solve the nonfactor central-sequence cocycle equation.

lessons.title: Central triviality and the core-inner kernel
lessons.summary: For a separable AFD type III0 factor, central triviality is equivalent to an inner canonical extension. Finite orbit partitions and measurable phase witnesses give the full kernel theorem and its formulation in every faithful-state chart.

lessons.title: Classification by factors, relations and flows
lessons.summary: AF principal relations and AFD factors share a complete classification by type labels and measured flows. The full dictionary includes every semifinite case and explains which automorphism information the flow forgets.

lessons.title: A continuous section of the module map
lessons.summary: A Radon-Nikodym correction lifts every flow automorphism coherently. Full crossed-product and core calculations give a continuous section of the module map and the resulting topological semidirect product.

lessons.title: Joint obstructions and outer conjugacy
lessons.summary: A shared central change of the return implementer defines a joint characteristic class. The full analytic hypotheses give outer-conjugacy classification, while an explicit torus-flow example shows that separate classes lose the scalar outer phase.

lessons.title: Modular time and the outer center
lessons.summary: Finite tensor implementers approximate modular time on the entire predual. The modular-time circle is the center of the approximately inner outer quotient and of the full outer group; the module circle is a separate quotient.

lessons.title: Crossed products from modular return data
lessons.summary: Every integer crossed product of a Powers factor is determined from its corrected modular return data. The full calculation includes the factor types, the exact torus-quotient flow, and the diffuse central circle with its homogeneous factor.

lessons.title: Pullbacks of the intrinsic invariant
lessons.summary: The modular return tuple of a Powers-factor automorphism is recovered from the equivariant pullback of its intrinsic invariant. Characteristic cocycles reconstruct the extension, including zero return and nonfaithful integer actions.

lessons.title: Modularly invariant Powers subfactors
lessons.summary: Every specified periodic faithful normal semifinite weight on a separable type III-lambda factor admits a unital invariant AFD subfactor of the same type. Exact weighted matrix blocks construct its Powers model, and fixed centralizer coordinates retain the original flow and weight in the infinite-mass case.

lessons.title: Amenable actions on AFD factors
lessons.summary: The marked intrinsic pullback, its module and its full characteristic class classify countable discrete amenable actions on every separable-predual AFD factor. Exact analytic inputs and a separate projective-implementer proof cover all factor types.

lessons.title: Ultraproduct corners and hypercentral tests
lessons.summary: Support corners preserve the exact norm of state commutators. The canonical-state centralizer and a diagonal bicentralizer identity describe the hypercentral test for general von Neumann algebras

lessons.title: Bicentralizers and the general hypercentral identity
lessons.summary: Expected separable subalgebras and measurable factor-fibre tests give the general bicentralizer-to-centralizer inclusion and the hypercentral identity

lessons.title: Bratteli reflection and the exceptional graph
lessons.summary: Path recurrences, explicit matrix-block inclusions and exact graph invariants distinguish a reflected Bratteli diagram from the rooted E8 tree.

lessons.title: Factorization, hereditary corners and quotient lifts
lessons.summary: Balanced factors and positive parts lift zero products through C*-quotients. Polar transport identifies hereditary corners, and primitive representations detect compact operators.

lessons.title: Representation fields and quasi-state duality
lessons.summary: Intertwiner-compatible operator fields recover the bidual. Finite Gram matching proves the quasi-state quotient theorem, and continuity recovers the original C*-algebra.

lessons.title: Pure states and common maximal abelian subalgebras
lessons.summary: Commuting positive contractions isolate finitely many orthogonal pure states. A maximal abelian subalgebra containing them has pure restrictions with unique state extensions.

prerequisites.contract: Arbitrary complex Hilbert spaces: completion, Riesz, bounded sesquilinear representation, adjoints and orthogonal projections.
Bounded C*-algebra continuous functional calculus, positive square roots, positivity and norm bounds.
Bicommutant theorem, bounded monotone nets, supports and bounded polar decomposition in arbitrary von Neumann algebras.
Ultraweak topology on bounded sets, separate multiplication continuity, normality of bounded positive maps equivalent to preservation of bounded increasing positive suprema.
General Hilbert spectral calculus for self-adjoint operators with exact Borel domains, bounded rectangular polar decomposition, finite-measure convergence and compact continuous approximation.
Conjugate-linear adjoints, closed operator graphs, analytic elements and strip/KMS arguments in the exact generality needed.
Enough states to detect positivity in arbitrary nonzero unital C*-algebras, including their norm-one property.
C*-bidual universal enveloping von Neumann algebra, canonical embeddings, isometric normal bidual inclusions, and same-norm weak-star-continuous second adjoints preserving compositions.
Bounded self-adjoint spectral projections inside a von Neumann algebra and norm approximation by spectral step functions.

Positive bounded maps between von Neumann algebras: preservation of bounded increasing positive suprema iff ultraweak continuity, with the positive same-norm preadjoint; provided by NP-04 at the recorded written-foundation boundary.
Concrete predual isometric duality, positive predual separation and span, normal-functional supports, inherited corner topology and ultraweak operations.
Sigma-strong and sigma-strong-star continuous duals equal the predual, with equal convex closures including the real self-adjoint versions.
Real/complex Hahn–Banach extension and locally convex separation, Banach–Alaoglu, weak compactness of Hilbert balls and Krein–Smulian for dual Banach spaces.

For the real-line and planar scalar integrals used in MA: Lebesgue integral bounds, sequential monotone and dominated convergence, absolutely integrable Fubini, the stated injective Borel changes of variables, finite-interval calculus, and integration by parts with integrable terms and verified endpoint limits. The exact source conditions and original application bridges are retained in the analytic packet.
scope_exclusions: No arbitrary net form of dominated convergence.
No operator-norm measurability of a merely strongly continuous orbit.
No Bochner integration in a general incomplete locally convex space.

prerequisites.contract: For the scalar functions used in MA: rectangle and circle Cauchy formulas, local power series and primitives, rectangle Morera and its triangle application, identity on connected open sets, the boundary maximum principle on finite rectangles, and the original simple-pole calculation for the centered rectangles in MA05 and MA15. No arbitrary-cycle residue theorem is imported.
scope_exclusions: No arbitrary-cycle or homological residue theorem.
No unbounded-strip maximum theorem without the boundedness assumption retained in MA.
No Stone or modular theorem is used.

prerequisites.contract: For every standard form (M,H,J,P) of an arbitrary von Neumann algebra, every normal semifinite faithful weight phi, and every directed net alpha_i in Aut(M) converging to alpha in the u-topology (norm convergence of f composed with alpha_i to f composed with alpha for every normal functional f), put C_phi(beta,t)=[D(phi composed with beta inverse):Dphi]_t. For every vector eta in H and every compact K in the real line, the supremum over t in K of ||(C_phi(alpha_i,t)-C_phi(alpha,t))eta|| tends to zero, and the same holds after taking adjoints. No separability, sigma-finiteness, faithful state, countable state family, ordered weights, bounded densities or strongly convergent inner lifts are assumed. The zero algebra is included.

Standard sigma-finite measurable Hilbert fields of separable complex fibres, including zero and variable dimensions; countable fundamental sections and measurable dimension strata; measurable scalar products, Gram-Schmidt and projections onto subspaces with specified measurable fundamental sections; bounded operator-field action, adjoints and norms; conjugate and direct-sum fields; bounded decomposable operators characterized as the commutant of the diagonal algebra; exact Hilbert direct-integral L2 spaces, finite-measure localization and almost-everywhere subsequences.
prerequisites.why_needed: DI uses the standard-base specialization of these precise foundation bindings and the distinct local DF constructions. No whole DI or foundation course is imported into DF.

prerequisites.contract: For a separably acting von Neumann algebra and a specified abelian von Neumann subalgebra of its center: a standard sigma-finite central decomposition with that subalgebra diagonal; countable-core localization for specified vector and operator families; fibrewise decomposable commutants and bicommutants; and almost-everywhere identification of two decompositions over the same diagonal structure.
prerequisites.why_needed: DC supplies all four CENTRAL clauses used by DI at its declared elementary and FIELD inputs.

prerequisites.contract: Countable rational star cores give measurable closed right-multiplier graphs, fundamental product pairs and left von Neumann-algebra generators. Full-fibre unitary isomorphisms have an explicit Borel code and completed measurable implementation. A locally bounded proper-original-algebra witness requires an explicitly analytic defect relation; Borel original membership is sufficient. The former unrestricted defect clause is refuted; the printed fullness converse has a conditional counterexample under CH.
prerequisites.why_needed: DI-05/07/09 use explicit algebra cores; DI-14 uses full-fibre Borel unitary coding; DI-08 needs the explicitly analytic defect hypothesis. DI-13 constructs full fibres and uses only the unconditional implication.

prerequisites.contract: Locally compact Hausdorff group analysis at arbitrary cardinality: left Haar Radon measure and its inversion/modular formulas, C_c-density and compactly supported approximate identities in L2, Radon product measure with L2 tensor identification, and nonunital Stone-Weierstrass for C0(G). For the real-line specialization, the continuous-character classification and compact-uniform topological identification are imported from existing HA-LCA-02 Theorem3.1 through the parameter reflection t mapped to -t.
prerequisites.why_needed: The existing OA-FND-HM and OA-FND-SW programme lessons contain the complete Haar, modular, Radon-product, tensor, approximation and C0 proofs. The local compact-support argument is a specialization.

prerequisites.contract: Every commutative complex C*-algebra, unital or nonunital, is isometrically *-isomorphic to C0 of its locally compact Hausdorff spectrum through its Gelfand transform; for a unital algebra the spectrum is compact.

For any locally compact Hausdorff space X, every positive real-linear functional on real C_c(X) is represented by a unique Borel measure finite on compact sets, outer regular on all Borel sets and inner regular on open sets; the representing integral complexifies. Inner regularity also holds on sigma-finite Borel sets. No compactness, metrizability, separability or sigma-compactness assumption on X is imposed.

Scalar Borel measure theory for standard Borel groups: finite and sigma-finite Radon–Nikodym derivatives and uniqueness, sigma-finite Tonelli/Fubini with Borel parameter integration, a countable Borel generator, and finite-partition L1 density. The joint derivative selection and its almost-everywhere convergence are proved in PF-38.
prerequisites.why_needed: PF-37–40 use rowwise scalar derivatives, product-null sections, parameter integration and a finite Borel partition approximation. The sigma-finite RN reduction is a separate input; the joint selection is proved locally.

prerequisites.contract: Standard-Borel Lusin–Souslin image theorem; compact inner approximation of finite Borel measures on Polish spaces; a Borel-isomorphism-to-Polish-group continuity principle; compact-group representation decomposition into finite-dimensional irreducibles. The regular-representation embedding, compact-neighborhood argument, category proof, and factor obstruction are given locally in PF-41–44.
prerequisites.why_needed: PF-41–44 recover a locally compact topology from a nonzero invariant Borel measure and compare it to existing Polish topologies.

prerequisites.contract: For a faithful normal semifinite weight on any von Neumann algebra, global domination of X↦φ(aXa*) by φ is equivalent to a bounded modular negative-half-strip extension with endpoint norm at most one; under that condition, the right GNS action on every x in n_φ is Λ_φ(xa*)=J_φ σ^φ_{-i/2}(a) J_φ Λ_φ(x). Include the exact support-corner reduction for a nonfaithful normal semifinite weight.
prerequisites.why_needed: ACI-01's forward and finite-cone conclusions use the exact analytic right-action theorem. The ACI-02/03 counterexample is independently computed and already refutes the printed reverse direction in the faithful case.

prerequisites.contract: Scalar real-line Plancherel, compact approximate identities, and the Weyl/multiplication commutant, including vector-valued Plancherel for arbitrary Hilbert multiplicity under Lebesgue measure; these are the exact harmonic inputs to the concrete dual average.
prerequisites.why_needed: OE-01–07 reconstruct IX.4.18 at arbitrary von Neumann generality without IX.4.20's false reverse direction.

prerequisites.contract: For an already existing faithful normal semifinite operator-valued weight T:A_+→B_hat_+, and any faithful normal semifinite scalar weight φ on B, the composite φ_hat◦T is n.f.s. and its modular group restricts to σ^φ on B. Only this forward direction is imported; it cannot depend on compatible-pair reconstruction.
prerequisites.why_needed: OE-01–07 reconstruct IX.4.18 at arbitrary von Neumann generality without IX.4.20's false reverse direction.

prerequisites.contract: For an n.f.s. trace τ on arbitrary semifinite Q, every normal weight on Q, including weights with a nonzero infinite part, is uniquely τ(h·−) for h in the full extended positive cone; the correspondence is additive, order preserving and normal.
prerequisites.why_needed: OE-01–07 reconstruct IX.4.18 at arbitrary von Neumann generality without IX.4.20's false reverse direction.

prerequisites.contract: For normal extended-positive operator-valued weights and a compatible real-line dual action, positive orbit integration commutes with normal extension and equivariant operator-valued maps on the entire extended positive cone; equality is checked against each positive normal functional, including infinite values.
prerequisites.why_needed: OE-01–07 reconstruct IX.4.18 at arbitrary von Neumann generality without IX.4.20's false reverse direction.

prerequisites.contract: For arbitrary n.f.s. scalar weights φ,ψ, the -i graph of u_t=[Dψ:Dφ]_t σ_t^φ has the exact oriented mixed finite-ideal identity ψ(az)=φ(zb), two-sided GNS ideal bounds, and extended-positive half-strip domination in the orientations of OR.6; include the necessary and sufficient graph criterion.
prerequisites.why_needed: The forward modular restriction and relative-cocycle lifting in OR03.

prerequisites.contract: For an existing n.f.s. OVW, finite-domain matrix positivity places dot T(y*z) in the oriented mixed scalar ideal and identifies its scalar extension on the finite overlap; right spectral cutoffs extend the identity to every scalar GNS product without a countability assumption.
prerequisites.why_needed: The forward modular restriction and relative-cocycle lifting in OR03.

prerequisites.contract: For normal complex-linear isometric groups with pointwise sigma-weakly continuous real orbits on an arbitrary unital von Neumann algebra inclusion, graph inclusion at -i implies equality of the real actions on the smaller algebra. Entire approximants and finite Blaschke-product uniqueness establish the comparison without prior invariance.
prerequisites.why_needed: The forward modular restriction and relative-cocycle lifting in OR03.

prerequisites.contract: Von Neumann type decomposition and trace structure used in IX.4 Exercise 1: corners of semifinite and type-I algebras, absence of finite projections in type III, sigma-strong discontinuity of involution on an infinite corner, normal trace densities in type I, and the integrable-density centralizer cutdown lemma.
A von Neumann algebra is atomic exactly when its predual has the Radon-Nikodym property; trace classes and their l1-sums have that property, and it passes to closed subspaces.
